comparison: Both evaluate the core TP signature identification (C7-C11). OpenEval emphasizes RNAseq methodology and RT-qPCR validation with specific donor numbers. Peer review focuses on the compelling evidence and reproducibility of the in vitro model. Both rate as SUPPORTED with strong agreement.

OpenEval R1 includes RT-qPCR validation claims (C72-C77) that peer R6 also addresses. Both confirm the validation of TP signature genes and EP2/EP4 receptor agonist effects. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both evaluate the correspondence between in vitro TP stimulation and RA pathogenic phenotypes (C78-C80). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (hypergeometric p-value, Monte Carlo). Peer review praises the model's accuracy in reflecting molecular mechanisms. Both SUPPORTED with strong concordance.

Both address scRNAseq analysis and mapping to RA clusters (C12-C13, C81-C84). OpenEval notes some speculation about 'new functional subset' interpretation. Peer review explicitly praises the mapping methodology as 'compelling' and 'informative.' Both SUPPORTED despite OpenEval's minor reservation.

OpenEval R4 addresses gene set activity analysis and mutually exclusive expression patterns (C82-C84, C113, C115-C116). Peer R2 covers overlapping claims about TP signature mapping. Both accept the in vivo validation through reference mapping despite acknowledged limitations. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate the identification of TP signature in specific RA monocyte subsets and mutual exclusivity with IFN signatures (C113, C115-C116). Peer review particularly praises the detailed comparisons with published datasets. Both SUPPORTED with strong agreement.

Both address chromatin accessibility and TF cooperation mechanisms (C14-C17). OpenEval details ATACseq methodology (HOMER, ChromVAR, TOBIAS). Peer review confirms the mechanistic finding of AP-1, CEBP, NR4A cooperation with NF-κB. Both SUPPORTED with complete agreement.

OpenEval R5 includes epigenomic analysis claims (C89-C96) that peer R9 addresses. Both confirm the robust validation of transcriptomic findings through complementary ATACseq approaches. Both SUPPORTED with methodological concordance.

Perfect claim overlap (C85-C88) on EP2/EP4 agonist and cAMP signaling validation. Both confirm the mechanistic link between cAMP and dichotomous inflammatory outcomes. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status with identical claim coverage.

Both evaluate IFN-γ suppression of TP genes (C18-C23). OpenEval emphasizes the selective suppression of ~27% of TP genes. Peer review confirms IFN-γ opposes PGE2 effects and accepts the dichotomous regulation. Both SUPPORTED with strong concordance.

OpenEval R7 includes claims (C97-C99) about IFN-γ effects that peer R10 also addresses. Both confirm IFN-γ's opposing effects on PGE2-induced gene expression. Both SUPPORTED with agreement on the regulatory mechanism.

Both address IFN-γ increasing expression of PGE2-suppressed genes (C24-C25). OpenEval emphasizes opposing regulation of different TNF-induced gene sets. Peer review confirms the dichotomous effects. Both SUPPORTED with concordance.
OpenEval R8 includes claims (C100-C101) about IFN-γ effects on ISGs that peer R10 addresses. Both confirm IFN-γ increases TNF and chemokines like CXCL10. Both SUPPORTED with agreement.

Both evaluate IFN-γ interaction analysis showing selective suppression of PGE2-induced genes while sparing NF-κB targets (C102-C104). Both confirm the mechanistic insight. Both SUPPORTED with complete agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C105-C112) on ATACseq analysis of IFN-γ suppression of PGE2-induced chromatin accessibility and TF activity. Both confirm the mechanistic findings using multiple complementary approaches. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Perfect claim overlap (C26-C29) on mutually exclusive TP and IFN signature expression in vivo. OpenEval notes causality cannot be definitively established from correlative data. Peer review accepts the in vivo validation and praises the expanded RA/ICI-RA comparison. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C1-C6) on background claims establishing knowledge gap. Both confirm these accurately summarize prior literature with appropriate citations. Both SUPPORTED as valid background context.

Perfect claim overlap (C30-C50) on PGE2 biology background claims. Both confirm these accurately summarize established knowledge with appropriate citations. Both SUPPORTED as valid background providing study context.

Perfect claim overlap (C51-C61) on background claims about PGE2-TNF crosstalk relevance. Both confirm these accurately represent prior literature establishing foundation for current study. Both SUPPORTED as appropriate background.

Perfect claim overlap (C62-C71) on ICI-arthritis background claims. Both confirm these accurately summarize established knowledge establishing clinical relevance. Both SUPPORTED as valid background context.

Both address speculative interpretations and therapeutic implications (C114, C117, C119, C124, C130). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, praising clinical relevance of biomarker suggestions. Key disagreement: OpenEval more conservative on speculative claims.

High overlap (C118, C120-C122, C125-C129) on discussion claims integrating findings with prior knowledge. Both confirm these accurately contextualize results and provide therapeutic context. Both SUPPORTED as valuable discussion points with clinical applications.
